items.title: The Price of a Chance in Artificial Societies
items.summary: Rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled autonomous agents to interact, coordinate, and pursue individual goals in artificial societies. However, our understanding of how reward structures shape their competitive behavior and collective outcomes remains incomplete. We simulate 200 LLM agents competi…

items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. items.summary: Multi-step Web tasks often require several LLM agents to gather and combine evidence. items.summary: Long-horizon consistency is essential for video world models, yet it becomes difficult to maintain once observed content falls outside the context window. items.title: SEAL: Sealed Queries for Local Sanitization against Indirect Prompt Injection
items.summary: Indirect prompt injection threatens local LLM agents through untrusted tool outputs, motivating defenses that suppress attacks while preserving task evidence under limited inference budgets. We introduce SEAL, which learns a soft prompt and scoring readout offline to sanitize tool outputs using a frozen task model. SE…

items.title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. Yet problem solving in unfamiliar domains calls for tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning, beyond factual retrieval and aggregation or learning solely from a preassembled…

items.title: Sticky Collusion: Persistence of LLM Agent Collusion after Incentive Removal and Partner Replacement
items.summary: We ask whether collusion between AI agents survives once formed, when its incentive is removed or a colluder is replaced. items.title: InterA11y: Interactive Web Accessibility Error Detection with LLM Agents
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown potential to expand the coverage of web accessibility evaluation. However, current LLM-based checkers neglect much of the interactive and dynamic web contexts, resulting in limited coverage, high false discovery rates, and inconsistent performance across models. items.title: ATLAS-Bench: An Agentic Tool-Use Benchmark for Local Area Search
items.summary: Reliable local search is essential for LLM agents to support everyday decisions and longer plans by finding places that meet users' needs at given times and locations. Yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of whether search results satisfy mandatory requirements, account for preferences, and ground factual…

items.title: Context Compaction for World Models
items.summary: World models let observers explore and interact with generated worlds. Recent work shows that when observers revisit a region, current models often fail to regenerate it consistently. We view this as a context retrieval problem. LLM agents manage context retrieval at two layers of their stack. At the model layer, the…

items.title: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate
items.summary: Multi-agent debate systems require agents to retain and revisit arguments across multiple rounds, yet limited context windows and unstructured memories make relevant information increasingly difficult to recover. items.title: Stratum: Repository Memory for Coding Agents Beyond the Context Window
items.summary: Context windows have grown a thousand-fold, yet coding agents still start every session with no memory of their past work. items.title: Context Is a Pipeline, Not a Window: Information Attrition in LLM Agent Harnesses
items.summary: LLM agents are judged by two numbers: the size of the context window, and how often the final answer is correct. Both numbers miss a third thing: how much of a tool's output is lost before the model ever sees it. We measured this loss in a real tool-using agent. items.title: MarkovSim: an LLM Agent Harness with Bounded Context for Long-Horizon Computational Simulation
items.summary: Recent studies have applied large language model (LLM) agent systems to computational simulation workflows. Fixed sonnet, opus and haiku on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error mid-session instead of switching to an older model when the newest is not yet available to the account or region
Self-hosted runner: Fixed an MCP server's on/off switch sometimes being lost when a session moved to a new machine
[Cloud sessions] Added a form card to cloud sessions, so you can fill in or decline a form an MCP server asks for instead of the request being canceled without you seeing it
Fixed MCP servers that also work without sign-in showing "needs authentication" after their stored sign-in stopped working; they are now used signed out
[VSCode] Fixed "Clear authentication" for MCP servers reporting success when the saved sign-in could not be removed
Changed OpenTelemetry mcp_server.name to report the real name of fixed-URL remote MCP servers declared by plugins from the official Anthropic marketplace, instead of custom
Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading
Fixed long hidden thinking being cut off as idle on Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, where the endpoint sends thinking progress updates

Changed ultrathink in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic's API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks letting a tool call through when Git Bash is missing and the hook's command is only quoted strings, such as a quoted path
Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions

Fixed hooks that run in PowerShell not blocking when the hook's program exits with code 2, and on Windows PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks with "shell": "powershell" failing open when Git for Windows isn't install…
Changed the /claude-api skill to build Managed Agents subagent teams on multiagent_20261001 with dynamic workflows on by default, instead of coordinator
Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in claude -p on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in
Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab
Improved the time to the first reply in cloud sessions when one of the desktop app's MCP servers can't connect
Improved artifacts with several views: Claude now routes each view on the link's #name and no longer says the address bar stays the same as you switch views
Fixed artifact publishes and updates being refused for some ordinary pages, such as pages with certain minified scripts or artifacts Claude could not read first
Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's
Fixed sessions failing turn after turn with "Invalid effort level" when an organization's admin caps a model's effort: Claude Code now lowers the effort, retries, and says which level it uses
Fixed the spinner, OpenTelemetry effort values and transcripts naming a newly picked effort level during a task before the model applied it; they now show the level in force

Changed automatic model switches after a flagged message to also cover model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names; set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK=1 to turn them off
[Cloud sessions] Added an effort level to the model picker when you create or edit a routine that runs in the cloud
Changed /code-review to tell Claude to put the effort level first and use max only when asked
**tools:** keep $ sequences literal in memory tool str_replace
**docs:** improve the descriptions of the code execution tool and its encrypted results
**mcp:** remove the stray await from the async tool_runner examples
**client:** link the Bedrock and Vertex raw response docstrings to the SDK documentation
**tools:** leave the tool runner's history to the caller after append_messages(), and keep the current reply out of the set_messages_params() callback
**tools:** keep running the tool runner's function tools when set_messages_params() gives tools as definitions, and stop running one it takes out of tools
**tools:** give the set_messages_params() callback of a tool runner its tools as definitions again
**tools:** keep a tool runner's betas, user_profile_id and workspace_id when set_messages_params() leaves them out
**docs:** improve the descriptions of the code execution tool and its encrypted results
**tools:** copy the messages a tool runner is created with again
**tools:** restore what the tool runner does after setMessagesParams() or pushMessages() in the loop body
**docs:** add credential expiry descriptions to the Managed Agents API reference
**docs:** improve Managed Agents memory store descriptions
**docs:** improve Managed Agents vault and credential descriptions
